reason: The attractions need powered movement, so I'll install the motor; it's the only available action.
expectation: I expect the motor to mount on the whale, though it will still need connections to the attractions.

effect: The motor is mounted; it still needs connections to drive the attractions.
reaction: A straightforward installation, with no further detail yet.
reason: The flexible coupler should connect the motor to the dragon's crank, and it's the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect it to link the motor to the dragon's crank shaft, though the stars may need a separate drive.

effect: The dragon now has a motor drive; the star theatre still needs its connection.
reaction: The coupler's result is clear, though it gives no mechanical detail.
reason: The reducing belt drive is the only combination offered and may give the stars their different speed.
expectation: I expect the belt drive to connect the star theatre at a reduced speed, though its exact arrangement is uncertain.

effect: The belt drive gives the star wheel a slower speed than the dragon, using a larger driven pulley.
reaction: The pulley explanation makes the different speeds easy to understand.
reason: The clear cover should guard the moving drive, and it's the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect the cover to protect the belt and pulleys while leaving them visible.

effect: The drive is now guarded; it appears ready to be switched on.
reaction: A straightforward safety fitting, with no extra detail.
reason: The switch key is the only combination offered and should let me test the attractions.
expectation: I expect the motor to run the dragon and star wheel at their different speeds, though I don't know what the test will show.

effect: The test confirms that both attractions work at different speeds and that the clutch slips if the dragon is held still; everything is switched off for the lifting test.
reaction: Seeing the two effects work together was satisfying, and the slipping clutch was a useful surprise.

mostWorthwhile.text: The reducing belt drive was most worthwhile: its small and large pulleys explained clearly how the stars could move more slowly than the dragon.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the motor and fitting the cover felt routine, with little detail in their results.

surprise.text: The clutch slipping when the dragon was held still added a safety feature I had not anticipated.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, although every step offered only one combination, so there were no meaningful choices between constructions.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see the whale's lifting test, although I would hope for more decisions than this chapter offered.
